top_stories.title: AI capital-spending fears become the market's main swing factor
points: Meta declined to give 2027 capital expenditure (capex — money spent on data centers, chips and other long-lived assets) guidance, triggering another post-earnings sell-off on worries about runaway AI infrastructure costs.
AMD's Q2 report Tuesday is the week's key read on AI accelerator (GPU — the specialized chips that train and run AI models) sales, data center demand, gross margins and forward guidance.

SK hynix analyst coverage begins this week as the post-IPO quiet period ends, making memory-chip demand from hyperscalers (giant cloud operators like Amazon, Microsoft and Google) a live indicator of the AI capex cycle.
Risk case: if major chipmakers signal hyperscalers are pulling back on AI spending, a broad equity selloff could follow.
Money is rotating out of compute-heavy tech toward large caps with scale, operational leverage and clear shareholder-return plans and no AI infrastructure bets.

unique_angles.point: Multiple semiconductor reports in the same week give a thematic read on whether AI infrastructure spending stays robust or moderates.
Frames it as an investing lesson: valuations are being destroyed by heavy AI spending with uncertain returns, and investors should hunt overlooked large caps with durable advantages instead.

items.title: July jobs report (Friday) tests Fed rate-cut odds
points: Economists forecast 88,000 jobs added in July, up 54% from June's 57,000, suggesting labor-market stabilization.
Unemployment rate is expected to hold steady at 4.2%.
Weak data could pull forward Federal Reserve rate cuts; strong data could delay them.
Also due: Fed Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (bank lending standards) Monday and NY Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations Friday.

items.title: SpaceX posts first public quarterly earnings (Tuesday)
points: Inaugural report as a public company, with focus on Starlink (its satellite internet service) subscriber growth and revenue trajectory.
Starship launch timeline updates are seen as critical to the valuation.
Capital spending plans will show how aggressively it funds Starlink, Starship and commercial services at once.
Elon Musk is expected on the call, a likely source of market-moving headlines.

items.title: Heavy earnings calendar across sectors
points: Monday: Palantir (AI/data software) and Snap (social advertising).
Tuesday–Wednesday: Merck, Pfizer, Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk (GLP-1 obesity drugs), Uber and Disney.
Thursday–Friday: ConocoPhillips, Airbnb, Shopify, plus Cloudflare and Warner Bros. Discovery.
Take-Two Interactive details the November launch of Grand Theft Auto VI on Friday; the Ai4 conference in Las Vegas Tuesday features OpenAI, Waymo and Cisco speakers.

items.title: Starbucks turnaround accelerates under new leadership
points: Global comparable-store sales (sales at locations open at least a year) rose 7.9%, a fourth straight quarter of growth and well above expectations.
Adjusted earnings of $0.85 per share beat the $0.66 consensus on cost cuts and better store operations.
Operating margin expanded to 14.4% from 10.1%.
Full-year guidance was raised; the CEO credited restaurant basics and afternoon service expansion, with the stock near its July 2021 record high.

items.title: Coca-Cola grows on brand strength and volume
points: Net sales rose 7% year over year to $13.4 billion; comparable EPS jumped 11% to $0.97.
Global unit case volume rose 5%, with namesake Coca-Cola volume up 5% and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar up 16%.
Powerade volume rose 8% and Diet Coke plus Diet Coke Light rose 7% combined.
CFO said Diet Coke is 'having a moment,' pointing to multiple simultaneous growth drivers.

issues.subject: Morning Brief: An important investing lesson from the tech stock dumpster fire

headlines: Meta's refusal to provide 2027 capital spending guidance triggered another earnings sell-off, highlighting investor fears about runaway AI infrastructure costs across tech.

Starbucks delivered 7.9% global comparable-store sales growth and expanded operating margins to 14.4%, proving that operational fundamentals and afternoon service focus can outperform AI-focused strategies.

Coca-Cola posted 7% net sales growth and 11% earnings-per-share growth with 5% volume increases, demonstrating that consumer staples with strong brand momentum are rewarding shareholders while tech struggles.
The market is rotating away from compute-heavy tech stocks toward large-cap companies with scale, clear shareholder value strategies, and no AI infrastructure bets.

sections.title: Starbucks Turnaround Accelerates Under New Leadership
points: Fourth consecutive quarter of same-store sales growth with 7.9% global comparable-store sales, far exceeding Wall Street expectations.
Adjusted earnings of $0.85 per share beat analyst forecasts of $0.66, driven by cost-cutting and improved store operations.
Operating margin expanded to 14.4% from 10.1%, signaling sustainable profitability gains from business fundamentals rather than one-time cuts.
Company raised full-year guidance and CEO attributed success to focusing on restaurant basics and afternoon service expansion.

sections.title: Coca-Cola Capitalizes on Brand Strength and Volume Growth
points: Net sales climbed 7% year-over-year to $13.4 billion, with comparable earnings per share jumping 11% to $0.97.
Global unit case volume surged 5%, with flagship Coca-Cola brand volume up 5% and Coca-Cola Zero Sugar accelerating at 16% volume growth.
Secondary brands also performing strongly: Powerade up 8%, Diet Coke and Diet Coke Light combined up 7%, showing broad portfolio momentum.
CFO noted Diet Coke is currently 'having a moment,' indicating shift in consumer preferences driving multiple growth drivers simultaneously.

sections.title: Key Investment Lesson: Fundamentals Over AI Speculation
points: Tech stock valuations are experiencing destruction due to excessive capital spending on AI infrastructure with uncertain returns.
Market is rewarding large-cap companies with proven operational leverage, strong management execution, and shareholder-value focus regardless of AI exposure.
Starbucks stock approaching July 2021 record highs despite no AI involvement, while AI-heavy tech names face persistent sell pressure.
Investors should redirect focus from daily AI stock obsession toward researching overlooked large-cap companies with durable competitive advantages.
